Position Summary 		   Total Duration 70   working  days
Note: Payment shall only   be  made after submission   of  a report   and  relevant deliverables   for  each milestone,   to  be reviewed   and  approved by   the  National Malaria Program.
Objective   and  Justification
The primary objective   of  hiring   a  Technical Assistant (TA)   is  to   support  the establishment   of  harmonized common master   data  across   the  MIS, TB, HIV, laboratory, logistics,   and  other relevant health   program  systems.
The specific objectives   are  to:
• Assess   existing  master   data  structures, reference data, identifiers,   and  coding systems used across relevant programs   and  platforms.
• Harmonize common master   data  for health facilities, administrative divisions, population, laboratory,   and  stock/commodities.
• Support validation   and  quality assurance   of  harmonized master data.
• Establish practical mechanisms   for  updating, maintaining,   and  exchanging common master   data  across systems.
• Provide technical recommendations   to  support secure   and  sustainable interoperability.
Scope   of  Work
The selected TA   will  work closely   with  the Head   of  the MIS Unit   and  relevant CNM teams,   program  focal points,   and  designated technical counterparts   from  TB, HIV, laboratory, logistics,   and  other relevant programs.   The  TA   will  review   existing  systems   and  data structures, identify common master   data  requirements, harmonize datasets,   and  support validation   and  integration.
Duties & Responsibilities:
•  Assessment   and  Planning
•  Review   the  existing MIS architecture, database structure, relevant modules, master data,   and  current   data  exchange mechanisms.
•  Identify relevant systems   and  databases used by TB, HIV, laboratory, stock/logistics,   and  other health programs.
•  Assess   data  availability, structures, standards, identifiers, update mechanisms, access requirements,   and  technical readiness.
•  Identify duplication, inconsistencies, gaps,   data  quality issues,   and  interoperability challenges.
•  Develop   a  proposed methodology   and  implementation plan   for  master   data  harmonization.
•  Master   Data  Harmonization   and  Standardization
•  Review   and  harmonize health facility names, codes, types, locations,   and  other relevant attributes.
•  Review   and  harmonize province, district, commune, village,   and  other relevant administrative references.
•  Review population reference   data  and geographic relationships required   for  program planning   and  reporting.
•  Review laboratory facility, service, test, specimen,   and  other relevant reference data.
•  Review   and  harmonize stock   and  commodity information, including RDTs, ACTs, LLINs, laboratory commodities,   and  other relevant commodities.
•  Define common identifiers, codes, naming conventions, field definitions,   and  data standards.
•  Data Mapping   and  Interoperability
•  Develop mapping/crosswalk tables between common master   data  and program-specific codes   and  identifiers.
•  Define   data  elements, formats, relationships,   and  standards required   for  exchange.
•  Develop procedures   for  matching   and  maintaining consistency between datasets.
•  Provide technical specifications   for  using common master   data  through APIs   or  other   data  exchange mechanisms.
•  Data Quality Assurance   and  Validation
•  Establish validation   and  quality assurance rules   for  common master data.
•  Identify   and  address duplication, inconsistent naming, missing values, invalid codes,   and  other   data  quality issues.
•  Conduct technical testing   and  stakeholder validation   of  harmonized datasets.
•  Refine master   data  based   on  validation results   and  agreed stakeholder feedback.
•  Maintenance, Governance   and  Documentation
•  Define procedures   for  creating, updating, deactivating,   and  maintaining master data.
•  Develop technical   and  user guidance   for  maintaining common master data.
•  Provide knowledge transfer   to  relevant CNM   and  technical staff.
•  Expected Outputs
•  Harmonized master   data  framework covering facility, administrative   and  population information.
•  Master   data  mapping/crosswalk tables between common   and  program-specific datasets.
•  Harmonized   and  validated datasets prepared   for  appropriate use within   the  MIS   and  integrated systems.
•  Technical specifications   and  recommendations   for  API/data exchange   and  master   data  maintenance.
•  Documentation, governance recommendations,   and  knowledge transfer provided   to  relevant CNM staff.
Expected Profile of Candidates
Qualifications:
•  Bachelor's Degree   in  Computer Science, Information Technology, Information Systems, Software Engineering, Health Informatics,   Data  Management,   or  another   related  field
Work History:
•  Database management, information system development,   data  integration,   or  system interoperability for  5  years  as a minimum
Skills & Knowledge:
General & Technical Skills
•  Demonstrated experience   in  master   data  management,   data  mapping,   data  harmonization,   data  validation,   and  data quality assurance.
•  Strong knowledge   of  database technologies,   data  standards, APIs,   and  information system interoperability.
•  Knowledge   of  cybersecurity principles, including secure   data  exchange, access control,   and  protection   of  sensitive information.
•  Experience   with  health information systems   or  government information systems   is  an advantage.
•  Ability   to  work   and  coordinate effectively   with  multiple government institutions   and  technical stakeholders.
•  Familiarity   with  the health system   in  Cambodia   is  desired.
•  Experience   in  malaria, TB, HIV, laboratory, logistics,   or  public health information systems   is  desired.
